key_insight: pdfQA delivers a realistic, multi-domain PDF question-answering benchmark (2K human-annotated + 2K synthetic) annotated across ten complexity dimensions, enabling robust evaluation of QA systems on true PDF challenges like layout and modality.
problem_solved: Existing QA datasets largely start from plain text or narrow domains and do not capture PDF-specific phenomena (e.g., layout, multi-column text, embedded images, varied file types). pdfQA fills this gap by providing diverse, challenging, and realistic PDF QA pairs with explicit complexity labels.
method: Curate multi-domain PDF sources and generate two parallel datasets: real-pdfQA (2K human-annotated QA pairs) and syn-pdfQA (2K synthetic QA pairs).
Annotate each QA pair along ten complexity dimensions (e.g., file type, source modality, source position, answer type) to characterize difficulty and diversity.
Apply quality and difficulty filters to obtain validated, challenging subsets and evaluate system performance across those dimensions.
impact: Enables researchers and engineers to benchmark and improve document understanding models on realistic PDF difficulties (layout, multimodality, retrieval). This drives development of more robust, production-ready PDF QA systems.
visual_elements: Dataset composition chart showing real-pdfQA vs syn-pdfQA and domain breakdown (e.g., scientific, legal, manuals).
Radar or heatmap of the ten complexity dimensions illustrating distribution and co-occurrence of difficulty factors.
Annotated PDF example highlighting question, answer span/location, and modality cues (text, table, image) on the page.
Bar chart of model performance stratified by difficulty/complexity levels to show where models fail.
paper_title: pdfQA: Diverse, Challenging, and Realistic Question Answering over PDFs
paper_authors: Tobias Schimanski, Imene Kolli, Jingwei Ni, Yu Fan, Ario Saeid Vaghefi
